Create an AI employee

A colleague with a job description. Nine sections — six already have a safe default.

Building from scratch takes about ten minutes. If you want the same thing configured for you, hire the Sales Executive module instead — it arrives with these skills and tools already chosen, and you can change any of them afterwards. Go to Hire →
Identity & placement

This name signs every message they send, so a guest will read it.

Needed — it appears at the end of every message and on every call.
What a guest is told they are speaking to.
Decides whose queue their handovers land in. Sales is Anita and Ravi.
M M M M M
Only used inside Veerha — guests never see it.
Model & judgement

How sure they have to be before they answer without you. This is the setting that decides how much work reaches your queue.

Asks you when it is unsure
Currently 0.75 of 1 confidence — the setting the live app called Confidence gate (HITL).

Anything they are less than three-quarters sure of comes to Waiting on you instead of going out. On last month’s traffic that would have been 31 of 218 replies.

How closely they stick to your wording
Currently 0.2 of 1 — the setting the live app called Temperature.

Prices, dates and policies are quoted exactly as written either way. This only changes the sentences around them.

Which brain
Provider and model. Changing this changes cost and speed, not what they are allowed to do.

Fast answers in about 1.6 s and costs roughly 1 credit a reply. The model name is no longer typed by hand — a typo used to produce an employee that could not think at all.

Standing instructions

Read before every reply. Keep it to things that are always true — anything about one guest belongs in Memory.

318 characters. Longer is not better — every line is read on every reply and counts against the credit cost above.
Memory

What they are allowed to remember between conversations. Anything switched off here is forgotten the moment a thread ends.

Long term
Facts that outlive one conversation — “prefers the river-facing rooms”. 6 held today.
Conversation
Facts inside one thread, dropped when it closes. 21 held today.
Customer
Everything attached to one guest, including what they told you last year. 67 held today.
Department
Facts every Sales employee should know. Nothing held yet.
Company
True for every guest — “check-out is 11 am”. Widest reach, so it is off by default. Nothing held yet.

These are the same five scopes as Memory in the nav, spelled the same way. Switching one off here hides those facts from this employee only — it does not delete them.

Goals and measures

Optional, and the only part of this form about what they should achieve. One of each is filled in so the shape is visible.

Goals · 1
Answer every new enquiry within five minutes, day or night
A sentence you would say to a new hire. It is shown on their card and in the weekly summary.
Measures (KPIs) · 1
Median first reply — target under 5m, measured weekly
A measure needs a number, a direction and a period. Yours reads: lower is better, checked every Monday.
Playbooks (SOPs)

The steps to follow in a named situation. Optional, but a playbook is what stops them improvising on the awkward cases.

When a group of ten or more enquires
Take the dates and the headcount, quote nothing, and book a call with Anita the same day.
Needs a name before you can create them They start paused. Nothing is sent to a guest until you switch them on.

What it would bring back
Three facts, in this order

Asked for a river-facing room both times he has stayed · travels with his wife, no children · rang off last October when the rate went past ₹50,000. Two hundred other facts about him were not used because nothing in this thread touches them.

Held back — this looks like a credential Not given to the AI
A guest’s message contained a link with a long access key in it, and the qualifier stored the whole message as a fact. The value is masked here, it was never indexed, and it is not in the recall path. A secret in memory is a secret read back to the model on every reply.

Nothing at Department or Company scope yet

Both are empty because nothing has been written there — not because they are switched off. A company fact is true for every guest, like “check-out is 11 am”. A department fact is true for everyone in Sales, like “Ravi handles group bookings”.

Add a fact

Something the AI should know that it cannot work out from the records.

Customer is the default because it is the narrowest. Company reaches every conversation the AI has, so it asks you to confirm.
A fact without a guest cannot be brought back for one.
Write it as you would tell a colleague. Never paste a password, a key or a link with one in it — anything that looks like a secret is held back.
Normal is 0.6 of 1. Always mention it puts the fact in every reply about this guest, so it is for allergies and access needs, not preferences.

Every AI employee with Customer memory switched on will be able to use it. Two of your four have it on.

Memory is not Knowledge
Memory is what the AI noticed about a guest. Knowledge is what you wrote down for it to quote. A refund rule belongs in Knowledge — put it here and only one guest ever benefits.

On the call

The AI rings a new lead over WhatsApp to verify them, and answers when someone rings in

Nothing has actually been dialled. Calling is switched on and it has gone through the motions 28 times in the last 7 days, but the Voice Call API is in test mode, so no phone has rung. Every one of those 28 is in the delivery log marked as simulated. Switch it live →
AI voice calling

Hub running, WhatsApp Business connected — but the call adapter is in test mode

Attempted28
+22%
Last 7 days
Actually dialled0 Test mode
Median length— Nothing connected
Credits spent14
+9%
A simulated call still thinks

Every attempt, connected or not, is a row in Deliveries & tools with what was said and what happened.

Who it rings

Outbound only. Inbound calls are always answered and always create a lead.

Ring every new lead to verify them
Within two minutes of the enquiry arriving, and never outside your working hours
Which enquiries get a call
All ten places a lead can come from. Take one out and those leads are only messaged.
WhatsAppWebsite form PhoneEmail Booking linkInstagram FacebookWalk-in ReferralImported list
Smallest budget worth quoting
Below this, the AI books a call with you instead of quoting or refusing.
₹ per stay

₹12,000 is about two nights in your cheapest room. Leave it at 0 and every under-budget enquiry books a call.

How it behaves on the call

Six choices, and each caption is what the guest hears — not help text.

Reads details back
Which things it repeats before ending the call

Repeats a time, a name or a figure — the things that cost something if they are wrong. Never a preference.

Asks for
How much of your field list it works through

Their name and what they are after. Your other fields get asked only where they fit the conversation.

Turn length
How much it says at a time

A three-word answer gets a one-line reply. A talkative caller gets more.

Closes the call by
What it offers at the end

Where the guest can book themselves, it sends the link rather than taking a slot in your diary. It falls back to asking for a time when there is no link, or when they would rather talk.

Enquiries under your smallest budget
What happens when the money is not there

Someone whose budget is under your prices gets a call with the team instead of a no. The AI never sends them a payment link — a person decides what that booking is worth.

Talks about what you have available
Whether it sells on the call

Searches the catalogue and talks through what matches. A longer, more sales-led call, and about ⅓ more credits.

What it will never do

These are not settings. They hold whatever else is switched on, and each one is checked against the transcripts.

Never asks the same question twice Checked in 312 calls
Never pushes past a no — it says goodbye and writes down why 9 calls ended this way
Never invents a price — if it is not in your rate card it takes a message 4 handed to you
Says it is Veerha’s assistant in the first sentence, every time Required · cannot be switched off
Voice

Eight to choose from, thirty in all. Listen before you pick — this is the first thing a guest hears.

Female
Anika In use
Breezy, quick — the default, and the one on your 28 attempts
Nisha
Firm and unhurried. Reads numbers most clearly.
Sara
Youthful, informal. Suits a short verification call.
Nisha
Bright and warm. Longer sentences carry well.
Male
Rohan
Upbeat, brisk.
Aditya
Even and factual. The least chatty of the eight.
Ishaan
Firm, low. Good on a poor line.
Kabir
Lively, expressive. Can sound hurried on a long call.

All thirty speak English and Hindi. Nothing here names the engine that produces them — that is ours to change without changing your setup.

Shows as
Your WhatsApp Business number · +91 90000 99001
If nobody answers
Tries twice more, four hours apart, then sends a message instead
 3 attempts
Recording
On, and the guest is told in the first sentence. Kept 90 days, then deleted.
Longest call
It winds up politely and offers a callback rather than cutting off
 6 minutes
2 unsaved changes Smallest budget and turn length. Saved changes take effect on the next call, not the one in progress.

Lead nurture

Sent automatically after a lead arrives, and stopped the moment they reply or the deal closes.

Three of the four steps have never sent

WhatsApp only accepts free text within 24 hours of the customer’s last message. Every step after day 1 falls outside that window, so it needs an approved template and does not have one. 36 sends have been skipped since 1 September.

Sequence is on
7 leads on it — but only day 1 ever reaches them
Add new leads automatically
Every lead that arrives joins at day 0
The cadence
Day 1
Day 1 nudge Sends

Hi {first}, just following up on your enquiry — happy to help you find the right fit. Want me to share a few options?

Uses the approved template Day 1 nudge. Ran 38 times · 19 replied.

Day 3
Day 3 value Cannot send

Following up on your enquiry — here is what most guests ask about next.

No approved template. WhatsApp only allows free text within 24 hours of the customer’s last message. This step comes due on day 3, so it is skipped every time.

Day 7
Day 7 nudge Cannot send

Hi {first}, still interested? Happy to help whenever you are ready.

No approved template. Skipped 22 times since 1 September.

Day 30
Day 30 win-back Cannot send

Hi {first}, checking in — if you are still looking I would be glad to help.

No approved template. Skipped 14 times since 1 September.

The live product files this under Settings › Automation. A nurture cadence is outbound marketing, not a preference, so it moves here — next to the campaigns it shares an audience with. Logged in DEPARTURES.

Pricing

Your price list — one controlled source, kept exact. Veerha quotes these figures and no others.

Veerha quotes a figure only if it is on this list and marked quotable. Anything else it declines to price and hands to you — it never estimates, rounds or invents a number.
Where this list comes from

A Google Sheet your team already keeps. Veerha re-reads it on a timer and tells you what it found.

In sync
Last read
Today, 09:12 — 14 minutes ago
Rows read
24
Rows held back
1
Next read
In about 1 minute
One row was held back. "Riverside lawn, half day" has the word on request where its price should be, so it is not priced and Veerha will not quote it. Every other row came through. Show me the row →
Read-only access. Veerha never writes to your sheet.
Your sheet has seven columns. Column G, "Notes", is not read.
Stored encrypted and never shown again after you save it. Where to get one →
A price you change in the sheet reaches Veerha within 15 minutes.
Save first — reading now uses what is saved, not what is on screen.
Replace the list from a file

A one-off import for when the sheet is not the source. It replaces every price, so it goes through a preview first.

This replaces all 24 prices, not just the ones in your file. Anything missing from the upload stops being quotable. You will see every added, changed and removed line and have to confirm before a single price moves.
No file chosen · .csv or .xlsx, up to 2,000 rows
What the file must contain
Column Needed? What it decides
itemRequired The name a guest would recognise. Veerha matches a question against this.
priceRequired A plain number. A word here holds the row back, as it did above.
descriptionOptional What Veerha says about it when a guest asks what it includes.
unitOptional Per night, per guest, per trip. Blank means the price is for one of the thing.
currencyOptional Blank falls back to the workspace currency, ₹ INR.
activeOptional Setting it to no keeps the row on the list but stops Veerha quoting it. Blank means yes.

Departments

Four departments. Every request is routed to one of them by what it is about — 168 were routed last month.

A department decides who handles a request. It does not decide who can see one. Visibility follows reporting lines — a manager sees everyone reporting to them, and anybody without a manager sees only their own customers. That is set on the org chart, not here. Org chart › Reporting lines →
4 results
Where would this go?

Routing is a description and a handful of examples, so the only honest way to check it is to try a sentence. This is that.

No AI employee in this department — it would go to Imran Shaikh, who is off shift until 9 AM

Add a department

Two fields and a few examples. It starts routing the moment you save it, so it sits below the four that already work.

Write it as you would explain the job to a new hire. The router reads this, so vague descriptions mis-route.
massage spa package
One phrase per chip — how they are stored is our problem, not yours.
You can test it before anything reaches it.
Who sees what

Set once for the workspace. Two switches, both with a consequence.

Limit what each role sees
On. A member sees their own customers; a manager sees everyone reporting to them. Off, everyone in the workspace sees every lead, customer, opportunity and quotation.
Admins can read customers
Off. An admin runs the workspace — reading its customers is a separate decision, so it is a separate switch.
Owner
Every customer
Manager
Theirs, and their team’s
Member
Only what they own
Viewer
Only what they own
Admin
None

Anybody without a manager sees only their own customers — which is why an unplaced person on the org chart is an access problem, not a diagram problem.

Behaviour

What Veerha may do on its own, and where it stops and asks you

Operating brief

Every conversation is grounded in this, so the AI answers as Rivergrove and not as a generic assistant.

Rebuilds the brief from Teach Veerha. Your edits above are replaced, so the old version is kept in the change log.
Autonomy

Anything switched off here is brought to you instead of being decided.

Reply to new enquiries
218 times in the last 30 days · median 1m 40s
Share rooms and live availability
Only rooms that are actually free for the dates asked about
Book and reschedule calls
Checked against your working hours · 24 booked this month
Send a quote without your approval
Off. Every quote waits — including the 23 you approved unchanged last month.
Quote group rates
Off. This is why Priya Nair is sitting in your queue.
When it hands over

Each of these stops the automation and puts the thread in your queue.

Someone asks for a person 6 times this month On

Fields & qualification

One profile. It decides what the AI must establish before it calls a lead a deal.

Enquiry

A profile is what the AI should establish before it treats a lead as a deal — not a list of boxes to fill. A refusal settles a topic just as well as an answer does, and the AI stops asking either way. This is the order it asks in.

Default
1 Enquiry type enquiry_kind
A stay, an event, a company account or an agent. Everything the AI says next depends on this one.
133 settled · 35 still open

158 settled · 10 still open

A date, or a number of nights.
154 settled · 14 still open

A headcount. For a wedding this is the one number that decides the quote.
157 settled · 11 still open

“None” settles this as firmly as “two” does.

The only two numbers on this page. Both state what happens when they run out.

Rules

The numbers your automations judge a customer by, in one place.

This page holds thresholds — not triggers. What starts an automation is a keyword and a journey on Entry points; sending and waiting live on Sequences and Workflows.
Customer tiers

Lifetime spend at Rivergrove, in ₹ (your workspace currency). Tiers decide who a sequence treats as a regular and who the AI greets by name.

Premium above
Everyone below this is General.
₹ and above

18 customers are Premium today. Sequences may offer them a returning-guest rate without asking you.

VIP above
Must be above Premium.
₹ and above
Changed from ₹2,00,000. 3 more customers become VIP when you save — 7 in all. A VIP enquiry never waits for the AI: it goes straight to Waiting on you.
Mark inactive after
Any reply, call or booking clears it immediately.
months of no contact

23 of 142 customers are inactive at 6 months. They drop out of campaign audiences and stop counting towards your reachable list. Set it to 0 to turn this off entirely.

Three tiers, one spelling each: General · Premium · VIP. Anyone can set a tier by hand on a customer, and a manual tier is never overwritten by these numbers.

Developers

Everything needed to wire Veerha into your site, your CRM or your own tooling — and one place that holds the keys.

Everything on this page is working. The widget is live, both webhooks are receiving, and Meta verified your callback on 12 September. Nothing is waiting on you.
Keys 4

Four credentials, four different lifecycles — so they are one list that says, for each, what it identifies, how it travels and who can end it. A key is shown masked until you ask for it, and asking is recorded.

Workspace key In use
Identifies this workspace to the chat widget and the intake webhook. It travels in an X-Veerha-Key header — never in a URL, where it would land in browser history, your server logs and every referrer.
Created 1 Sep · last used 2 minutes ago · revealed twice, both by Anita
Storefront key — rivergrove.example.com In use
What your own website uses to read your catalogue and send you orders. Sent as the X-Storefront-Key header. One key per site, revocable on its own.
Reads your catalogue Takes orders
Created 18 Sep · last used 6 minutes ago · 412 calls today
WhatsApp verify token Verified
Whatever you typed into Meta, so Meta can prove the callback URL is yours. It is checked once, when you press Verify there.
Saved 12 Sep · Meta verified the callback the same minute
Meta app secret Held elsewhere
Signs each delivery from Meta so we can tell a real message from a forged one. It lives with the connection, not here.
Managed on Integrations › WhatsApp
Rotating replaces a key and gives you 24 hours. During that window both work; after it, anything still sending the old one is refused. Revoking is immediate and cannot be undone — use it if a key has been pasted into a chat, a ticket or a screenshot.
Website chat widget

Uses your logo, brand colour and name. Chats land in Conversations and the AI answers them live.

Live on 1 site
No key in this snippet. The site id is public on purpose — anything in your page’s JavaScript is published.
Lead intake webhook

Post a lead here and it is scored, a customer is created, and the Lead-Nurture workflow starts.

Daily spend cap

The most Veerha may spend in one day before it stops and asks you.

0 turns the cap off.

At the cap Veerha stops spending for the rest of the day: it finishes the thread it is in, starts nothing new, and moves everything waiting into Waiting on you with a note saying why. It never keeps spending quietly, and it never goes silent on a guest without telling you.
